newsitem.title: GERMANY: Daimler says sees stable 1997 workforce.
newsitem.headline: Daimler says sees stable 1997 workforce.

text.p: German industrial group Daimler-Benz AG said on Wednesday it expected to have a relatively stable workforce for 1997 after job cuts last year due to a major restructuring programme.
"The difficult times of staff reductions are over," Daimler management board member Heiner Tropitzsch told the group's annual news conference.
"At the end of 1997 we will have the same number of staff as at the end of 1996," said Tropitzsch, who is responsible for personnel issues at the Stuttgart-based group.

Daimler's workforce at the end of 1996 fell seven percent to 290,029 workers from 310,993 at the end of 1995, with the number of employees outside Germany dropping two percent to 67,208 in 1996 from 68,907 in 1995.
At the end of the first quarter, Daimler said its workforce totalled 287,636 workers compared with 292,478 at the end of the 1996 first quarter.
Many of the job cuts last year were due to Daimler's decision to end transfers to troubled Dutch aircraft Fokker and to merge the remains of electronics group AEG into the main Daimler structure.

Tropitzsch said "positive personnel developments" would take place in Latin America, where Daimler is expanding its Mercedes vehicle production, and also in the United States where Mercedes will soon begin building its new M-class sport utility vehicle in Alabama.
But he said job cuts may occur in the commercial truck unit due to difficult sales conditions and at Daimler's Dasa aerospace unit.
